digest.digest: Iran is reportedly preparing for a prolonged and potentially wider conflict, viewing recent diplomatic efforts as a potential cover for larger attacks by the US and Israel. Evidence suggests Iran is planning offensive actions, including potential attacks on enemy territory and targeting energy facilities of Gulf states if its own are targeted. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) is actively advising and assisting proxy militias in Iraq, Yemen, and Lebanon, with specific instructions provided for missile deployments and target lists. Iran's internal leadership appointments, such as the new IRGC commander, are seen as indicative of a readiness for sustained confrontation. The US faces a diplomatic deadline with Iran, with preliminary deals expiring and no broad agreement reached to end the war. This stalemate is impacting regional stability and has led to the Pentagon rotating aircraft carriers, highlighting the ongoing strain of the conflict. The war is also having significant economic consequences, affecting global oil prices and impacting the profitability of US transportation companies. China's energy strategy appears to be benefiting from the ongoing conflict, with its oil throughput showing a month-on-month rise. There are also reports of threats from the US, including potential military action against Oman, amid expiring agreements with Iran.

next_events.title: Iranian Military Escalation and Proxy Network Activation
next_events.description: Iran has explicitly stated its intention to escalate and has been preparing for a larger conflict, viewing US talks as a diversion. Analysts should monitor any increased activity by Iranian proxy militias in Iraq, Yemen, and Lebanon, particularly regarding missile deployments targeting the Red Sea and potential attacks on Gulf state energy facilities or critical infrastructure like internet cables.

next_events.title: Strait of Hormuz Offensive
next_events.description: Iran has threatened to go on the offensive in the Strait of Hormuz if diplomacy with the US fails. This critical chokepoint for global oil supplies remains a high-risk area. Watch for any naval maneuvers, increased military presence, or direct threats to shipping that could signal an imminent escalation.

next_events.title: US-Iran Economic Warfare and Diplomatic Breakdown
next_events.description: The failure to agree on a broad deal and the expiration of the preliminary memorandum of understanding indicate a complete breakdown in diplomatic efforts, with the conflict now shifting to an economic battle. Observe new US sanctions or economic pressure tactics, and Iran's retaliatory measures or responses to internal economic pain and potential unrest.

next_events.title: Internal Iranian Stability and Leadership Posture
next_events.description: Iran is bracing for conflict both abroad and at home, with its rulers wary of economic pain leading to internal unrest. The appointment of hard-liner Ahmad Vahidi as IRGC commander-in-chief signals a leadership committed to sustained confrontation. Monitor for signs of domestic dissent, protests, or any shifts in the rhetoric or actions of the IRGC leadership.

next_events.title: Regional Target Expansion and Israeli Actions
next_events.description: Iran fears US talks were a cover for an Israeli attack and has planned potential attacks on 'enemy territory,' including ground operations in Kuwait and threats against Gulf states. Watch for any intelligence indicating Iranian or proxy operations beyond current conflict zones, especially any actions perceived as pre-emptive or retaliatory against Israel or its allies.
